_metadata.rubric: owner-clarified rubric with calibration anchors + no-literal-false-facts reminder, 2026-10-18
_metadata.independence: I read only u29-blind-input.json and no other file, repository content, web source or API.

hints.reason: WATER: you swim in water; NIGHT: only via the loose phrase 'night swim', which is a scene but not a strong one.
WATER: glass of water; NIGHT: no recognizable route (a bedside glass of water is invented rescue).

best_available.why: Only hint touching both sides, via 'night swim'.

pairs.pair_note: Weak pair for these hints; no PASS. Something like MOONLIT/REFLECTION or TIDE might serve better.

hints.reason: WITCH: 'the witching hour' (ordinary inflection); NIGHT: the witching hour is the dead of night, plus 'night hours'.
Contains the target NIGHT as a substring, a rule failure, despite the good witching-hour route.
NIGHT: Halloween night; WITCH: the iconic Halloween witch costume/figure.

best_available.why: Broad shared scene that reaches both words instantly.

pairs.pair_note: MIDNIGHT must be dropped for containing NIGHT.

hints.reason: Contains the target WOLF as a substring, a rule failure.
WOLF: wolves howl; NIGHT: the familiar scene of a howl in the night.
NIGHT: the moon in the night sky; WOLF: the wolf howling at the moon image.

best_available.why: Classic image that ties both sides equally.

pairs.pair_note: WEREWOLF fails on substring.

pairs.pair_note: MARY is a variant route of LINER and leans on the same knowledge.

best_available.why: Ocean side is unmistakable and robotic subs are a familiar idea.

pairs.pair_note: Both moderate; neither is a giveaway.

hints.reason: ROCK: 'rock pool' compound (more British; US says tide pool); OCEAN: only indirectly, rock pools sit at the seashore.

pairs.pair_note: POOL is acceptable for UK players but weaker on the OCEAN side.

hints.reason: SALT: brine is salt water; OCEAN: 'the briny' / seawater is brine.

SALT: 'salt water'; OCEAN: ocean water.

best_available.why: Salt water / ocean water is clean and not a synonym giveaway.

pairs.pair_note: SEA is nearly a synonym of OCEAN; serve WATER first.

best_available.why: Real collocations on both sides.

hints.reason: SNAKE: serpent is a synonym; OCEAN: the legendary sea serpent.

best_available.why: Sea serpent links both, though serpent is a synonym of SNAKE.

pairs.pair_note: Both top hints are synonym-adjacent; EEL is the fairest non-giveaway.

hints.reason: SPIDER: 'sea spider' is a real but little-known animal; OCEAN: sea is a near-synonym.

best_available.why: Spider crab is fairly well known and crabs are clearly ocean animals.

pairs.pair_note: SEA leans on an obscure animal.

hints.reason: SPRING: 'spring water'; OCEAN: ocean water.

pairs.pair_note: BREAK reaches OCEAN only loosely.

hints.reason: STAR: Patrick Star (SpongeBob); OCEAN: he is a starfish living under the sea in Bikini Bottom.

pairs.pair_note: Good pair.
